decision.reason: Toomer (2019; shipped row 2422 year_r=2021; duplicate row 2456 removed) Experiment 2 (Ch. 4) conceptually re-tests Gitsaki’s (1999) specific empirical finding that previously encountered V+N collocations yield lower gap-fill scores than prep+N collocations. Section 2.1.1 (p. 9) attributes to Gitsaki (1999) an empirical study of 275 Greek junior high school learners tested on textbook collocations where gap-fill production was less accurate for V+N than prep+N. Experiment 2 tests 78 Chinese learners on 43 analysed (21 V+N, 22 prep+N) collocations repeated six times under bolded vs. unbolded reading; gap-fill accuracy was lower for V+N than prep+N when bolded (17.91% vs. 30.91%, z=-4.78, p<.001, Tables 15 & 19; p. 130 prose reverses this direction) but not unbolded (15.80% vs. 17.96%, z=-0.24, p=.99; interaction z=3.08, p=.002, Table 17). Section 5.3.6 (p. 163) explicitly states that Experiment 2 partially corroborates Gitsaki’s gap-fill ordering, distinct from general learnability claims (Howarth, 1998b; Ackerman & Chen, 2013), and notes no prior study compared enhanced and unenhanced L2 lexical and grammatical collocation learning. Shipped row 2422 represents only Sonbul & Schmitt (2013) (adj+N/N+N medical collocations), so Gitsaki (1999) is genuinely absent. Catalog and Google Books records (0236, ISBN 1573093890) verify the 1999 primary empirical book and its 275-learner blank-filling study, while its internal numeric rankings (and equivalence to the restricted 1996 thesis, not substituted here) are not independently read from the book body and rest on Toomer’s explicit attribution.
